subject: General Knowledge
topic: World Superlatives — Largest, Smallest, Highest, Longest

questions.stem: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering approximately 165 million km² — larger than all land masses combined. Ocean size order (decreasing): Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic.

questions.stem: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Vatican City (Holy See) is the world's smallest country by area at approximately 0.44 km² (110 acres), located within Rome, Italy. It is also the smallest by population (~800). Monaco is the 2nd smallest by area but most densely populated.

questions.stem: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: B is correct. The Nile River (Africa) is traditionally considered the world's longest river at approximately 6,650 km. Note: Recent measurements suggest the Amazon (South America) may be slightly longer, but the standard exam answer remains the Nile. Amazon is the largest by volume/discharge.

questions.stem: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Lake Baikal (Russia, Siberia) is the deepest lake in the world at approximately 1,642 m depth. It is also the world's oldest lake (~25 million years) and contains about 20% of the world's surface fresh water. Lake Tanganyika is 2nd deepest.

questions.stem: Which is the tallest building in the world as of 2024?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Burj Khalifa in Dubai, UAE, is the world's tallest building at 828 m (2,717 ft), completed in 2010. It has 163 floors. Note: Jeddah Tower (Saudi Arabia) under construction aims to surpass it at over 1,000 m.

questions.stem: Which country has the largest area in the world?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Russia is the largest country by area at approximately 17.1 million km², covering about 11% of Earth's total land area and spanning 11 time zones. Order: Russia > Canada > USA > China > Brazil.

questions.stem: Which is the highest plateau in the world?
questions.explanation: C is correct. The Tibetan Plateau (also called the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau) is the world's highest plateau, with an average elevation of about 4,500 m (14,800 ft) above sea level — earning the title 'Roof of the World'. It covers an area of about 2.5 million km² in China.

questions.stem: Which is the largest desert in the world?
questions.explanation: C is correct. A desert is defined by precipitation (less than 250 mm/year), not temperature. Antarctica is the world's largest desert at ~14.2 million km² — it receives almost no precipitation. Many students answer 'Sahara' (correct for hot deserts; 2nd largest overall). Exam tip: If question specifies 'hot desert', answer is Sahara.

questions.stem: Which country has the most number of natural lakes?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Canada has the highest number of natural lakes in the world, containing about 31,752 lakes larger than 3 km² and over 2 million lakes of all sizes. This represents about 60% of the world's natural lakes. Followed by Russia, USA, and China.

questions.stem: Which is the longest wall in the world?
questions.explanation: B is correct. The Great Wall of China is the longest wall in the world, stretching approximately 21,196 km (13,171 miles) including all sections from different dynasties. The main wall built by the Ming Dynasty is about 8,850 km. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

questions.stem: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Lake Superior is the world's largest freshwater lake by surface area at ~82,100 km². It is one of the North American Great Lakes. Note: Caspian Sea is larger by area but is saline (saltwater). Lake Baikal is largest by volume and deepest. Lake Victoria is Africa's largest freshwater lake.
